item.title: US Department of Labor secures court order requiring New Jersey employer to pay $700K in back wages, damages to 48 workers denied overtime pay
item.description: VOORHEES, NJ – The U.S. Department of Labor has obtained a consent judgment and final order in federal district court requiring a New Jersey drywall installer to pay $725,000 in back wages, damages, and civil money penalties after denying 48 workers overtime pay.The department’s Wage and Hour Division found that P & B Partitions Inc. failed to pay their employees for pre-shift work while they waited for transportation to their jobsites. The failure to pay constitutes a violation under the Fair Labor Standards Act’s overtime provisions. “Tasks completed to prepare for the job, and in this case, while waiting to get to the worksite, is work that must be compensated,” said Wage and Hour Division District Director Charlene Rachor in Southern New Jersey. “Failing to pay workers overtime wages deprives them of their rights, and we will hold employers accountable for such actions.”The consent judgment requires P & B Partitions Inc. to pay $350,000 in back wages, an equal amount in liquidated damages to 48 workers, and requires payment of an additional $25,000 in civil penalties. The judgment was entered in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey on June 26, 2026.“The U.S. Department of Labor will pursue legal action to ensure that all employees receive the compensation they are legally owed,” said Regional Solicitor of Labor Jeffrey S. item.title: US Department of Labor obtains consent order against retirement plan fiduciaries of defunct Chicago law firm for failing to distribute $6.4M in assets
item.description: CHICAGO – Following a complaint filed by the U.S. Department of Labor, a defunct Chicago law firm’s retirement plan distributed $6,498,858 in retirement plan assets to 40 employees. The plan’s fiduciaries failed to properly terminate the plan and disburse those funds as required by law.On Aug. 18, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, Eastern Division, entered a consent order resolving the department’s claims against the McCullough, Campbell & Lane LLP, and the firm’s capital partners David L. Joslyn, John W. McCullough, F. Dennis Nelson, and Paul S. Turner. The department alleged that the defendants violated the Employee Retirement Income Security Act by failing to follow a 2019 partnership resolution. The resolution required them to terminate the firm’s retirement plan and distribute the plan’s assets to employees. The defendants have provided proof that plan’s assets were distributed to participants, except for approximately $13,861 in the employer-level plan accounts. The consent order requires the plan’s recordkeeper to distribute those funds to its participants and to terminate the plan. “After their law firm closed, Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn failed to provide employees with their promised retirement benefits,” said Employee Benefits Security Administration Regional Director Kelli Hammerl in Chicago. “The Department of Labor helped participants gain access to their retirement savings.” The order permanently bars Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn from serving as fiduciaries or service providers for any ERISA-covered employee benefit plan. The plan transferred account balances belonging to plan participants it could not locate to the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation’s Missing Participants Program.Employers can get help complying with the law through EBSA’s correction programs, which includes the Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program. The plan’s fiduciaries failed to properly terminate the plan and disburse those funds as required by law.On Aug. 18, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, Eastern Division, entered a consent order resolving the department’s claims against the McCullough, Campbell & Lane LLP, and the firm’s capital partners David L. Joslyn, John W. McCullough, F. Dennis Nelson, and Paul S. Turner. The department alleged that the defendants violated the Employee Retirement Income Security Act by failing to follow a 2019 partnership resolution. The resolution required them to terminate the firm’s retirement plan and distribute the plan’s assets to employees. The defendants have provided proof that plan’s assets were distributed to participants, except for approximately $13,861 in the employer-level plan accounts. The consent order requires the plan’s recordkeeper to distribute those funds to its participants and to terminate the plan. “After their law firm closed, Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn failed to provide employees with their promised retirement benefits,” said Employee Benefits Security Administration Regional Director Kelli Hammerl in Chicago. “The Department of Labor helped participants gain access to their retirement savings.” The order permanently bars Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn from serving as fiduciaries or service providers for any ERISA-covered employee benefit plan. The plan transferred account balances belonging to plan participants it could not locate to the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation’s Missing Participants Program.Employers can get help complying with the law through EBSA’s correction programs, which includes the Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program. The VFCP allows plan officials to correct violations and avoid excise taxes for prohibited transactions. Employers and workers can contact EBSA at askebsa.dol.gov or call 866-444-3272 toll-free for help with private sector job-based retirement and health plans.

item.title: State of Maine v. Devon M. Stewart
item.description:
MAINE SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT Reporter of Decisions Decision: 2026 ME 104 Docket: Som-25-305 Argued: March 5, 2026 Decided: October 27, 2026

STATE OF MAINE
v.
DEVON M. STEWART
LAWRENCE, J. [¶1] Devon M. Stewart appeals from a judgment of conviction of one count of gross sexual assault entered by the trial court (Somerset County, Mullen, C.J.) after a jury trial.
